::: {#rem-why-cond-mean .remark}
#### Why the estimated conditional mean is the usual prediction

The prediction in @exm-prediction-cond-mean is chosen
because the conditional mean is the best possible prediction under squared error loss.
Among all functions $\modmem$ of the covariate,
$\condE{\Outvar}{\Predvar}$ has the smallest expected squared error
$\E{\sqf{\Outvar - \modmemf{\Predvar}}}$
([conditional mean minimizes squared-error risk](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#thm-best-predictor)).
The conditional mean is unknown,
so we estimate it from data and predict with the estimate.

The target depends on the loss.
For absolute error loss, the best prediction is the conditional median instead,
and other losses have other targets
[@hastie2009elements, p. 20].
:::
